text: What if a spider's web could actually stop a runaway train?
In Spider-Man 2, a hero shoots webs to stop a speeding subway train.
Most people call that pure movie magic.
But in 2012, three physics students actually ran the numbers.
Four subway cars at full speed need about three hundred thousand newtons to stop.
That's like holding up over thirty tons.
So the web has to be stiff, but stretchy enough to soak up the crash.
Real spider silk already does this. Weight for weight, it's stronger than steel.
And Darwin's bark spider spins silk more than ten times tougher than Kevlar.
That's almost exactly the toughness the students needed.
So the web in the movie isn't magic. It's just a really, really big spider.
